text:
The state holds a fee simple subject to a condition subsequent (also called a fee simple subject to a right of entry or power of termination). The grant uses "provided, however, that if... then the grantor... may re-enter," which is classic condition-subsequent language, and it does not automatically end the estate. Instead, the grantor or their successors hold a right of re-entry that they must exercise if the condition is breached.

CONFIDENCE: 88
